props.name: ariaCleanerLabel
props.description: Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) for the cleaner button, describing its action for screen readers.

props.name: ariaPickerLabel
props.description: Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) for the indicator button that toggles the options list.

props.name: className

These classes will be merged with the default React autocomplete classes.

props.name: cleaner
props.description:
Enables the cleaner: a button that empties the field, the selection and the text. It shows
when an option is selected and, unless `allowOnlyDefinedOptions` is set, when the field holds
text, never while the component is disabled or read-only. With `value` set, the field empties
once you take the `null` it reports. It stays out of the Tab order and gives the focus back to
the field.

props.name: clearSearchOnSelect
props.description:
Whether a pick, or <kbd>Enter</kbd> on text that names no option, empties the search the options
are filtered by, so the list opens in full next time. The field shows the picked option's label
either way.

props.name: container
props.type: Element | DocumentFragment | (() => Element | DocumentFragment | null) | null
props.description:
The element the dropdown is rendered into instead of `document.body`. Implies `portal`.
Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert.

props.name: defaultInputValue
props.description:
The text the field starts with and goes back to on a form reset, for example a value the user
typed earlier without picking an option. It filters the options like typed text, without a
hint. A selected option writes its label over it. Ignored when `inputValue` is set.

props.name: defaultShow
props.description: The initial open state of the uncontrolled dropdown panel — read once on mount.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
The initial selection for the uncontrolled mode: the value of the option to select, compared
as text, so `1` and `'1'` select the same option. It is applied as soon as the options contain
it, unless the user has picked, typed or cleared by then. Ignored when `value` is set.

props.name: disabled
props.description:
Toggle the disabled state for the component.
When `true`, the React.js autocomplete is non-interactive and appears visually disabled.
Users cannot type, select options, or trigger the dropdown.

props.name: feedback
props.description:
Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled
after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and
`feedbackInvalid` instead.

props.name: feedbackInvalid
props.description:
Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works
with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state.

props.name: feedbackValid
props.description:
Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with
client-side validation, where the browser decides the state.

props.name: floatingLabel
props.description: Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value.

props.name: floatingLabelAlways
props.description: Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty.

props.name: globalSearch
props.description:
Routes typing to the field from anywhere in the component, so a keystroke never depends on where
the focus sits. Set to `false` to keep it local: a keystroke then counts only while the field has
the focus.

props.name: highlightOptionsOnSearch
props.description:
Highlight options that match the search criteria.
When `true`, matching portions of option labels are visually highlighted
based on the current search input value.

props.name: id
props.description:
Set the id attribute for the native input element.
This id is used for accessibility purposes and form associations.
If not provided, a unique id may be generated automatically.

props.name: inputValue
props.description:
The controlled text of the field. The field shows this text and nothing else: typing, a pick
and the cleaner ask for a new text through `onInputChange`, so update `inputValue` there. A
text that is not the selected option's label filters the options like typed text. When `value`
is set as well, a `value` you change leaves the text alone: set both.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Mark the control invalid.
props.deprecated:
6.0.0 Use `validationState="invalid"` instead — `invalid` is ignored when
`validationState` is set.

props.name: label
props.description: Add a caption for a component.

props.name: loading
props.description: When set, the options list is marked busy and shows a row with a spinner and `loadingLabel` below its options while you fetch them; the options it shows can still be picked.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: Text of the loading row below the options, announced to screen readers when the shown list starts loading or the list shows up loading.

props.name: name
props.description:
Name of the text input the form posts. That input holds what the user sees, the selected
option's label or their own text when `allowOnlyDefinedOptions` is off, so
`{ value: 'ng', label: 'Angular' }` posts `Angular`, not `ng`. Without a name the
autocomplete is not submitted with the form.

props.name: onChange
props.description:
Execute a function when the selected option changes. Called with the option, or `null` when
the selection is cleared. Text the user types without picking an option is not a selection:
read it from `onInputChange`.

props.name: onHide
props.description:
The callback is fired when the dropdown requests to be hidden.
Called when the dropdown closes due to user interaction, clicks outside,
escape key, or programmatic changes.

props.name: onInput
props.description:
Execute a function when the search changes, the text the options are filtered by: as the user
types, and with an empty string when the autocomplete empties it, for example after a pick or
with the cleaner. Use it for external search; the text of the field comes through
`onInputChange`.

props.name: onInputChange
props.description:
Execute a function when the text of the field changes: as the user types, after a pick (the
option's label), with the cleaner, on a form reset, and when the selection changes from
outside. Pair it with `inputValue`.

props.name: onShow
props.description:
The callback is fired when the dropdown requests to be shown.
Called when the dropdown opens due to user interaction, focus,
or programmatic changes.

props.name: onShowChange
props.description:
Callback fired when the dropdown panel requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture
(Escape, outside click, option pick) or, in uncontrolled mode, any internal toggle. In
controlled mode update `show` yourself, or the panel stays as it is.

props.name: onValidationStateChange
props.description:
Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the text of the field, or the form is
reset, while `validationState` (or `invalid`/`valid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the
value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again.

props.name: options
props.description:
List of option elements.
Can contain Option objects, OptionsGroup objects, or plain strings.
Plain strings are converted to simple Option objects internally.
This is a required prop - the React autocomplete needs options to function.

props.name: optionsGroupsTemplate
props.description:
Custom template for rendering option groups.
Allows customization of how option group headers appear in the dropdown.
The function receives an OptionsGroup object and should return a ReactNode.

props.name: optionsMaxHeight
props.description:
Sets maxHeight of options list.
Controls the maximum height of the dropdown options container.
Can be a number (pixels) or a CSS length string (e.g., '200px', '10rem').
When content exceeds this height, a scrollbar will appear.

props.name: optionsTemplate
props.description:
Custom template for rendering individual options.
Allows complete customization of how each option appears in the dropdown.
The function receives an Option object and should return a ReactNode.

props.name: pickerIcon
props.description:
The button that opens the options menu: `true` for the built-in icon, a node for your own,
`false` for no button.
When `true`, displays a dropdown arrow button that can be clicked
to manually show or hide the options dropdown.

props.name: placeholder
props.description:
Specifies a short hint that is visible in the search input.
Displayed when the input is empty to guide user interaction.
Standard HTML input placeholder behavior.

props.name: portal
props.description:
Renders the autocomplete dropdown in a React portal, allowing it to escape the
parent container's styling constraints (like overflow, z-index, or positioning).
When enabled, the dropdown is rendered into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise
into `document.body`, so it appears above other page elements and isn't clipped by parent
containers.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
Toggle the readonly state for the component.
When `true`, users can view and interact with the dropdown but cannot
type in the search input or modify the selection through typing.
Selection via clicking options may still be possible.

props.name: required
props.description:
When it is present, it indicates that the user must choose a value before submitting the form.
Adds HTML5 form validation requirement. The form will not submit
until a valid selection is made.

props.name: resetSelectionOnOptionsChange
props.description:
Determines whether the selected options should be cleared when the options list is updated.
When `true`, any previously selected options will be reset whenever the options
list undergoes a change. This ensures that outdated selections are not retained
when new options are provided.

props.name: search
props.description: `'external'` hands the filtering to your code: the component shows the options you pass and reports what the user types through `onInput`.

props.name: searchNoResultsLabel
props.description:
Sets the label for no results when filtering.
- `false`: Don't show any message when no results found
- `true`: Show default "No results found" message
- `string`: Show custom text message
- `ReactNode`: Show custom component/element

Control the open state of the dropdown panel. When set, the panel renders what `show` says
and dismiss gestures only call `onShowChange` — nothing closes until the parent flips the
prop.

props.name: showHints
props.description:
Show hint options based on the current input value.
When `true`, displays a preview/hint of the first matching option
as semi-transparent text in the input field, similar to browser autocomplete.
Only text the user types gets a hint.

- `'lg'`: Large size variant
- `undefined`: Default/medium size

props.name: validationState

`aria-invalid` on the input and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the

it through `onValidationStateChange`.

props.name: value
props.description:
The controlled selection: the value of the selected option, or `null` (an empty string too) for
none. It is matched
against the option values compared as text, so `1` and `'1'` select the same option, and the
field keeps the label of a selected option that leaves `options`. Pair it with `onChange`; for
the uncontrolled mode use `defaultValue` instead.

props.name: virtualScroller
props.description:
Enable virtual scroller for the options list.
When `true`, only visible options are rendered in the DOM for better performance
with large option lists. Works in conjunction with `visibleItems` prop.

Controls whether the dropdown is initially visible.
The dropdown visibility can still be toggled through user interaction.
props.deprecated:

props.name: visibleItems

Amount of visible items when virtualScroller is enabled.
Determines how many option items are rendered at once when virtual scrolling is active.
Higher values show more items but use more memory. Lower values improve performance.

props.description: A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next month in the React Calendar component. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. Customize for a more accessible calendar experience.

props.name: ariaNavNextYearLabel
props.description: A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next year in the React Calendar component. Screen readers utilize this label to inform users of the button's functionality, aiding in a more inclusive application.

props.name: ariaNavNextYearsLabel
props.description: Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the next page of years.

props.name: ariaNavPrevMonthLabel
props.description: A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the previous month in the React Calendar component. This label is announced by screen readers, ensuring clarity around the button's purpose.

props.name: ariaNavPrevYearLabel
props.description: A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the previous year in the React Calendar component. Use it to enhance the experience for screen readers and further accessibility.

props.name: ariaNavPrevYearsLabel
props.description: Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the previous page of years.

props.name: ariaNothingToPickLabel
props.default: Nothing on this page can be picked
props.description: Sets the description (`aria-describedby`) of a grid in which nothing can be picked, such as a page wholly outside `minDate` / `maxDate` or one that `disabledDates` covers, also announced when the calendar turns to such a page. An empty string leaves the grid without a description.

props.name: ariaSelectedDateAnnouncement
props.description: Sets the message announced when a click or Enter / Space picks a date, and with `range` when both ends fall on the same day. `{date}` is replaced by the full name of what was picked, such as `Wednesday, August 12, 2026` or `August 10 – 16, 2026`. An empty string announces nothing.

props.name: ariaSelectedRangeAnnouncement
props.description: Sets the message announced with `range` when a pick leaves both ends set. `{start}` and `{end}` are replaced by the full names of its ends. An empty string announces nothing.

props.name: ariaWeekNumberLabel
props.description: Names each week number for screen readers: a function that takes the week number and returns its name. Without it the name is the locale's word for week and the number, such as `Week 36`. Keep the number in the name, so a voice-control user can say what they see.

props.name: calendarDate
props.description: Defines the initial date or reference date for the React Calendar component. This date can be either a Date object or a string that can be converted into a valid date.

props.name: calendars
props.description: Specifies how many individual calendars should be displayed side by side on desktop devices. Increasing this number allows your users to view multiple months (or years, etc.) simultaneously.

props.name: className
props.description: A string of all classNames you want to apply to the outermost container of the React Calendar component. Use this to style or theme your calendar.

props.name: dayFormat
props.description: Sets the format for days. Accepts either a built-in format ('numeric' or '2-digit') or a custom function to return any desired string or number for the day.

props.name: disabledDates
props.description: Specifies one or more dates that cannot be selected by the user. This is useful for disabling weekends, holidays, or any dates that you need to restrict within your React Calendar component. In week, month, quarter and year selection a period is disabled when every day of it is.

props.name: endDate
props.description: Defines the initially selected ending date (applicable when using range selection). Accepts both Date objects and valid date strings.

props.name: firstDayOfWeek
props.description:
Sets the first day of the week. This can be adjusted for different locales or preferences:
- `0` = Sunday
- `1` = Monday
- `2` = Tuesday
- `3` = Wednesday
- `4` = Thursday
- `5` = Friday
- `6` = Saturday

props.name: locale
props.description: Indicates the locale for the React Calendar component. If not explicitly provided, it inherits the locale settings from the browser.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: The maximum date that can be selected. The days after its day are disabled within the calendar, and a time of day it carries leaves its own day selectable. In week selection its whole week stays selectable. This is often used to restrict future selections.

props.name: minDate
props.description: The minimum date that can be selected. The days before its day are disabled in the calendar, and a time of day it carries leaves its own day selectable. In week selection its whole week stays selectable. Useful for preventing selection of past dates or creating limited booking windows.

props.name: monthFormat
props.description: Sets the format for month names. Accepts built-in formats ('long', 'narrow', 'short', 'numeric', '2-digit').

props.name: navNextDoubleIcon
props.description: Customizes the icon for navigating multiple steps forward (double jump), e.g., skipping multiple months or years at once. Ideal for quick navigation through large date ranges. In right-to-left it shows on the double previous button.

props.name: navNextIcon
props.description: Customizes the icon for navigating to the next view (month, year, etc.) depending on the current view. Accepts any valid `ReactNode`, enabling you to display text, images, or icons. In right-to-left it shows on the previous button.

props.name: navPrevDoubleIcon
props.description: Customizes the icon for a double jump backward (e.g., jumping multiple months or years at once). This feature simplifies larger date range navigation within your React Calendar component. In right-to-left it shows on the double next button.

props.name: navPrevIcon

props.name: columns
props.description:
Table columns configuration. When omitted, the columns are generated from the keys of the first item, skipping the keys that begin with an underscore.

Each array item is either a column name, a column object or a group of columns:
- `key` (required)(String) - the name of the item property the column displays.
- `label` (String) - the visible label of the column. When omitted, it is generated from `key` by splitting kebab-case and snake_case into words and capitalizing each of them.
- `sortable` (Boolean) - set to `false` to exclude the column from sorting.
- `sorter` (Function) - a custom comparator for the column, called with two items.
- `filterable` (Boolean) - set to `false` to remove the filter from the column.
- `filter` (Function) - a custom filter for the column, called with the column values, a change handler and the current filter state.
- `headerStyle` (Object) - inline styles for the column header (useful for defining widths).
- `headerProps` (Object) - properties for the column header cell.
- `cellStyle` (Object) - inline styles for every data cell in the column.
- `cellProps` (Object) - properties for every data cell in the column.
- `children` (Array) - columns grouped under one header; a group carries `label` and `children` only.

- multiple (Boolean) - Enables sorting by multiple columns simultaneously. The sorting order will be maintained across multiple columns based on the order of interaction.
- resettable (Boolean) - If set to true, clicking on the sorter cycles through three states: ascending, descending, and null (no sorting). The third click on the sorter will reset the sorting and restore the table to its original order.

Prop for table columns configuration. If prop is not defined, table will display columns based on the first item keys, omitting keys that begins with underscore (e.g. '_props')

In columns prop each array item represents one column. Item might be specified in two ways:
String: each item define column name equal to item value.
Object: item is object with following keys available as column configuration:
- key (required)(String) - define column name equal to item key.
- label (String) - define visible label of column. If not defined, label will be generated automatically based on column name, by converting kebab-case and snake_case to individual words and capitalization of each word.
- _props (Object) - adds classes to all cels in column, ex. `_props: { scope: 'col', className: 'custom-class' }`,
- _style (Object) - adds styles to the column header (useful for defining widths)
